title: Stanley Kubrick
subtitle: the thirteen features, plus A.I.
blurb: The thirteen features in release order, the early shorts as optional rows, and Spielberg's A.I. as a coda — about 31 hours.
notes: Kubrick developed it for years and handed the project to Steven Spielberg, who wrote and directed it after Kubrick's death in 1999. It closes this list by request, and it appears on the Spielberg list as well.
Fear and Desire is here even though Kubrick disowned it.
He thought it amateurish and tried to keep it from being shown. It is still his first feature, so the list keeps it.
From Wikidata, in hours — the thirteen features alone are about 27 of the 31. The generator refuses to build without a runtime for every row.
Filmography from Wikipedia's Stanley Kubrick filmography; runtimes and release dates from Wikidata.

sections.title: New York
sections.intro: A Look magazine photographer teaching himself to make films: three documentary shorts, two features financed with money raised from family and friends, and a first studio picture with producer James B. Harris. The shorts are optional rows.

items.note: His first feature — disowned by Kubrick, who tried to keep it out of circulation

sections.title: Hollywood
sections.intro: Four studio pictures: two produced with Harris, one he was hired onto, and one made after the partnership ended. Lolita onward was shot in England, and England is where he stayed.

items.note: A hired job, and the only feature he made without final control
In full: Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb

sections.title: England
sections.intro: Six films in thirty-one years, made from outside London with the control he had been working toward, the gaps between them widening from three years to twelve.

sections.title: Coda
sections.intro: Kubrick spent years developing A.I. and handed the project to Steven Spielberg, who wrote and directed it after Kubrick's death. It closes this list by request.

items.note: Steven Spielberg's film, developed by Kubrick for years and handed on — here by request; it is on the Spielberg list too
